advice:
Potato: early blight, severe (about 45% of the leaf).
A fungal leaf disease of potato, found in both hills and plains. It is worse in dry, warm weather with rain now and then, and in weak or poorly manured crops.
Much of the leaf area is affected. Spray soon and get advice from your KVK on the next steps.
What to do:
- Plant only disease-free seed tubers.
- Collect and destroy infected plant debris. Spores left in the soil start the next infection.
- Give the crop balanced manure and fertiliser. Weak crops get this disease more.
If you need to spray, use one of these:
- Mancozeb 75% WP: 600 to 800 g in 300 litres of water per acre, do not spray in the last 10 days before harvest
- Chlorothalonil 75% WP: 350 to 500 g in 240 to 320 litres of water per acre, do not spray in the last 10 days before harvest
- Copper oxychloride 50% WP: 1 kg in 300 to 400 litres of water per acre, do not spray in the last 6 days before harvest
Read the label on the pack before you mix anything, and use only the dose on the label or the dose your KVK gives you.
Wear gloves, a face mask and a cap while mixing and spraying. Cover your feet and hands.
Please show the plant to your nearest KVK (Krishi Vigyan Kendra) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551 (free call).

label: potato_late_blight
raw:
Here is the rewritten advice:

Potatoes are susceptible to late blight, a fast-spreading disease that spreads in cool, cloudy, very humid weather with rain. Infected tubers carry the disease from one crop to the next. Water-soaked spots on leaves grow bigger, turn purple-brown and then black. Remove and destroy the spotted leaves now and spray to protect the rest of the crop. Plant healthy seed tubers and never store visibly infected tubers. Grow resistant varieties such as Kufri Naveen, Kufri Jeevan, Kufri Alankar, Kufri Khasi Garo, Kufri Moti or Kufri Girdhari.

advice:
Potato: late blight, severe (about 45% of the leaf).
A fast-spreading disease of potato leaves, stems and tubers. It spreads in cool, cloudy, very humid weather with rain. Infected tubers carry it from one crop to the next.
A large part of the crop is affected and the tubers are at risk. Contact your KVK today.
What to do:
- Plant healthy seed tubers and never store visibly infected tubers.
- Grow resistant varieties such as Kufri Naveen, Kufri Jeevan, Kufri Alankar, Kufri Khasi Garo, Kufri Moti or Kufri Girdhari. Short-duration varieties also help.
- Keep the field well drained and avoid waterlogging.
If you need to spray, use one of these:
- Mancozeb 75% WP: 600 to 800 g in 300 litres of water per acre, do not spray in the last 10 days before harvest
- Dimethomorph 50% WP: 400 g in 300 litres of water per acre, do not spray in the last 10 days before harvest
- Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP: 600 to 800 g in 200 to 300 litres of water per acre, check the waiting period on the label
Read the label on the pack before you mix anything, and use only the dose on the label or the dose your KVK gives you.
Wear gloves, a face mask and a cap while mixing and spraying. Cover your feet and hands.
Please show the plant to your nearest KVK (Krishi Vigyan Kendra) or call the Kisan Call Centre on 1800-180-1551 (free call).
